provenance.manuscript: PWR-Scan: A Complete Detection Theory and Algorithm for Structured Frequency-Covariance Change

dcase.interpretation: The external DCASE check did not demonstrate discrimination. It is retained as negative evidence, not reframed as validation.

proofEntries.label: Assumption 2.1
proofEntries.title: Smooth conditional response
proofEntries.statement: For u0 = E[U], V = U - u0 and tau^2 = E[V^2], every conditional log-power response g_k is twice continuously differentiable on an interval containing the support of U, with sup |g''_k| <= L_k, and E[V^4] is finite.
proofSteps: This is the regularity hypothesis used to control the Taylor remainder; it is not inferred from the observations used by the test.
proofEntries.conclusion: The loading ell = g'(u0) and a finite fourth-moment remainder bound are well-defined.
proofEntries.boundary: Smoothness and the fourth moment must be justified or calibrated for the intended acoustic regime.

equations.alt: ell equals the derivative of g at u zero

proofEntries.label: Proposition 2.2
proofEntries.title: Rank-one approximation of log-power covariance
proofEntries.statement: Under Assumption 2.1, the current-minus-baseline feature covariance decomposes as tau^2 ell ell^T + E, and the operator norm of E is bounded by conditional-residual drift plus the cross and quadratic Taylor remainders.
proofSteps: Expand g(U) at u0 and center the Taylor remainder.
Use E[xi | U] = 0 to remove residual cross-covariances.
Bound E[V r-bar], Cov(r-bar), and rank-one cross terms by Cauchy-Schwarz and the operator norm identity for outer products.
proofEntries.conclusion: The acoustic model supplies a quantified rank-one leading covariance term rather than an exact factor claim.
proofEntries.boundary: If the remainder bound is of the same order as tau^2 ||ell||^2, a rank-one interpretation is not warranted.

equations.alt: covariance difference equals a rank-one term plus an operator-norm-bounded remainder

proofEntries.label: Proposition 2.3
proofEntries.title: Directional spike survives model mismatch
proofEntries.statement: If the baseline-whitened block contrast is vartheta u u^T + E_B with ||E_B||op <= eta, its leading relative-covariance eigenvalue is at least 1 + vartheta - eta. When vartheta > eta, the pooled-whitened effect has the stated strictly positive lower bound.
assumptions: Positive signal margin vartheta > eta for the pooled positive lower bound
proofSteps: Insert u into the Rayleigh quotient.
Apply |u^T E_B u| <= ||E_B||op.
Use monotonicity of x/(1 + pi_1 x) to translate the baseline-relative gap into the pooled-whitened effect.
proofEntries.conclusion: The conservative effective signal is (vartheta - eta)+, mapped monotonically to the pooled parameter.
proofEntries.boundary: The result supplies no positive-signal guarantee when eta >= vartheta.

equations.alt: when vartheta is greater than eta, the pooled effect is bounded below by vartheta minus eta divided by one plus pi one times vartheta minus eta, which is positive

proofEntries.label: Assumption 3.1
proofEntries.title: Stratified cluster exchangeability
proofEntries.statement: Conditional on observed strata and pre-fixed folds, the complete cluster-level data object has the same distribution under every label-preserving transformation in the allowed group.
proofSteps: This is a design or distributional invariance condition. Permutations move entire recordings, never individual frames.
proofEntries.conclusion: The cluster is the inferential unit for exact randomization.
proofEntries.boundary: Cluster length, sensor, deployment and observed covariates must not create label-dependent laws within a stratum.

equations.alt: D is equal in distribution to g D for every allowed transformation g

proofEntries.label: Proposition 3.2
proofEntries.title: Covariance equality is not exchangeability
proofEntries.statement: Outside a common Gaussian law, equal covariance does not imply invariance under label permutation; even Gaussian groups with different means can share covariance while violating cluster exchangeability.
proofSteps: Choose two laws with identical covariance but different means or fourth moments.
Their joint law changes after labels are swapped.
Re-centering changes the statistic but cannot create invariance of the raw data law.
proofEntries.conclusion: Finite-sample exactness applies to the full-law or design-based null, not a covariance-only null.
proofEntries.boundary: A covariance-only null requires a separately proved studentized asymptotic or bootstrap procedure.

proofEntries.label: Proposition 3.3
proofEntries.title: Approximate level with guard gaps
proofEntries.statement: For a stationary beta-mixing process split into N equal clusters separated by guard gap g, Berbee coupling bounds rejection probability by alpha + (N - 1) beta(g), provided the independent-copy randomization test has level alpha.
assumptions: A usable external bound on beta(g)
proofSteps: Couple clusters sequentially to independent replicas.
A union bound limits any coupling mismatch to (N - 1) beta(g).
On the no-mismatch event, the dependent-data decision equals the exact independent-copy decision.
proofEntries.conclusion: Dependence costs an explicit additive level error.
proofEntries.boundary: A visually small sample autocorrelation is not evidence that beta(g) equals zero.

equations.alt: null rejection probability is at most alpha plus N minus one times beta of the guard gap

proofEntries.label: Definition 4.1
proofEntries.title: Block PWR matrix and local statistic
proofEntries.statement: For each candidate block, whiten the sample covariance difference by the pooled sample covariance and take its largest eigenvalue.
assumptions: Invertible pooled covariance on every candidate block
proofSteps: This is the local statistic definition; symmetry makes its spectrum real and its Rayleigh quotient explicit.
proofEntries.conclusion: Large T_B is evidence for a positive current-state covariance component.
proofEntries.boundary: A data-selected ridge is outside the primary theorem unless the full selection rule is included and re-proved.

equations.alt: D B is the pooled-whitened sample covariance difference and T B is its largest eigenvalue

proofEntries.label: Proposition 4.2
proofEntries.title: Exact monotone correspondence with Roy's root
proofEntries.statement: If lambda_k are the generalized eigenvalues of the current and baseline covariance pair, the PWR eigenvalues are h(lambda_k) = (lambda_k - 1)/(pi_0 + pi_1 lambda_k), and h is strictly increasing.
proofSteps: Use the same generalized eigenvector for the difference/pooled pair.
Symmetric whitening preserves generalized eigenvalues.
Differentiate h to obtain a strictly positive derivative.
proofEntries.conclusion: Within a block, PWR and Fisher-Roy orderings and one-sided rejection regions coincide exactly.
proofEntries.boundary: The pooled representation is a reparameterization, not a claim of a new empirical root.

equations.alt: each PWR eigenvalue is a monotone transform of its generalized eigenvalue and T B is h of Roy's root

proofEntries.label: Remark 4.3
proofEntries.title: Re-expression, not a new empirical statistic
proofEntries.statement: Pooled whitening is selected to keep the whitening matrix fixed across permutations and expose the power analysis; it does not discard Roy-root information.
proofSteps: The claim follows from the strict monotonicity established in Proposition 4.2.
proofEntries.conclusion: Local rank and one-sided rejection order are unchanged.
proofEntries.boundary: This equivalence is block-local and does not remove the need to calibrate the global maximum.

proofEntries.label: Definition 4.4
proofEntries.title: Theory-derived block scale
proofEntries.statement: Each block is normalized by the effective-sample scale containing direction cost, weighted search cost, and the second-order matrix-concentration term.
assumptions: Pre-fixed weights w_B > 0 with sum at most one
proofSteps: This definition packages the terms later obtained from Gaussian covariance concentration and a weighted union bound.
proofEntries.conclusion: Different block widths become comparable on a common theoretical noise scale.
proofEntries.boundary: Weights are complexity allocations, not posterior signal probabilities, and cannot be tuned after viewing the test data.

equations.alt: a B equals the square root direction term plus square root weighted search term plus a second-order term

proofEntries.label: Definition 4.5
proofEntries.title: One-layer PWR-Scan
proofEntries.statement: The global statistic is the maximum of T_B/a_B over the pre-fixed candidate family, calibrated once by the permutation distribution of that complete maximum.
assumptions: Candidate family, weights, preprocessing and numerical rules fixed before analysis
proofSteps: This definition places block dependence and search multiplicity inside one randomization statistic rather than a second min-p layer.
proofEntries.conclusion: The method performs one global upper-tail rank calculation per analysis.
proofEntries.boundary: Data-dependent candidate additions must be repeated inside every permutation or treated as a new procedure.

equations.alt: Z B is T B divided by a B and S PWR is the maximum Z B

proofEntries.label: Assumption 5.1
proofEntries.title: Full exchangeability
proofEntries.statement: Under the global exchangeability null, the complete data object is distributionally invariant under every element of the allowed finite transformation group.
proofSteps: This is the invariance premise for the finite-group rank argument.
proofEntries.conclusion: Every orbit position is probabilistically interchangeable under the null.
proofEntries.boundary: Equality of covariance alone does not imply this condition.

equations.alt: D is equal in distribution to h D for every h in the transformation group

proofEntries.label: Remark 5.2
proofEntries.title: Two null models have different roles
proofEntries.statement: In the common Gaussian model, equality in law and equality of covariance align, allowing exactness and minimax analysis in one experiment; outside it, exactness requires the stronger full-law null.
proofSteps: Contrast the common-Gaussian special case with non-Gaussian equal-covariance counterexamples.
proofEntries.conclusion: Finite-sample exactness and covariance-only inference must not be conflated.
proofEntries.boundary: Studentized asymptotic randomization or bootstrap validity is a separate theorem.

proofEntries.label: Definition 5.3
proofEntries.title: Full-permutation PWR p-value
proofEntries.statement: The p-value is the proportion of distinct orbit assignments whose complete global statistic is at least as large as the observed statistic; ties use the conservative greater-than-or-equal rule.
proofSteps: This is the exact orbit-rank definition used by the level theorem.
proofEntries.conclusion: Reject at level alpha exactly when the orbit p-value is at most alpha.
proofEntries.boundary: The p-value grid cannot resolve values below one over the orbit size.

equations.alt: the PWR p-value is the orbit fraction with statistic at least the observed statistic

proofEntries.label: Lemma 5.4
proofEntries.title: Randomization rank lemma
proofEntries.statement: For a finite group acting on an invariant random object, the upper orbit rank of any measurable statistic is super-uniform.
proofSteps: Condition on the orbit.
Invariance makes the observed orbit position uniform.
At most a u fraction of orbit positions can have conservative upper rank at most u; stabilizers and ties only increase ranks.
proofEntries.conclusion: P(p_S <= u) <= u for every u in [0,1].
proofEntries.boundary: The lemma proves validity, not power or sharpness of the random critical value.

equations.alt: the probability that p S is at most u is at most u

proofEntries.label: Theorem 5.5
proofEntries.title: Finite-sample global level
proofEntries.statement: Under full exchangeability and identical application of the complete analysis function to every orbit element, PWR-Scan controls the global rejection probability at alpha for any sample size, dimension, candidate family and dependence among blocks.
assumptions: Same complete measurable analysis on every assignment
proofSteps: Treat the already-maximized scan as one measurable statistic.
Apply Lemma 5.4 to its orbit rank.
No blockwise union bound is needed because maximization is inside S.
proofEntries.conclusion: The global test is finite-sample level alpha under the explicit exchangeability null.
proofEntries.boundary: Exactness does not extend automatically to unequal full laws with equal covariance.

equations.alt: the worst-case null rejection probability under the exchangeability null is at most alpha

proofEntries.label: Corollary 5.6
proofEntries.title: Gaussian finite-sample exactness
proofEntries.statement: Independent samples from one common zero-mean Gaussian distribution satisfy Theorem 5.5 whenever every pooled block covariance is invertible; no asymptotic ratio condition is required for validity.
assumptions: Invertible pooled covariance on every block
proofSteps: A pooled sample from the common Gaussian law is exchangeable in its labels.
Invoke Theorem 5.5.
proofEntries.conclusion: The Gaussian reference experiment inherits finite-sample global level control.
proofEntries.boundary: Exact size alpha additionally depends on a continuous orbit statistic and alignment of alpha with the orbit grid.

proofEntries.label: Definition 5.7
proofEntries.title: Monte Carlo PWR p-value
proofEntries.statement: With R independent uniform transformations, the randomized p-value adds the observed assignment as one exceedance and divides by R + 1.
assumptions: Transformations sampled independently of the data and uniformly from the allowed group
proofSteps: This is the plus-one corrected finite-sample definition.
proofEntries.conclusion: The smallest possible Monte Carlo p-value is 1/(R + 1), never zero.
proofEntries.boundary: Removing either plus one invalidates the finite-sample calibration.

equations.alt: the Monte Carlo p-value is one plus the exceedance count divided by R plus one

proofEntries.label: Theorem 5.8
proofEntries.title: Finite-sample validity of random permutations
proofEntries.statement: Under full exchangeability, independent uniform random transformations with the plus-one correction produce a super-uniform p-value and hence a level-alpha test.
proofSteps: Introduce an independent uniform reference group element G0.
Conditional on the orbit, the R + 1 transformed statistics are exchangeable.
The conservative upper rank of the reference statistic is super-uniform; relative transformations recover the implemented p-value law.
proofEntries.conclusion: Monte Carlo randomization retains finite-sample validity for every R.
proofEntries.boundary: Validity can coexist with no rejection resolution when R + 1 < 1/alpha.

equations.alt: under the exchangeability null, the probability that the Monte Carlo p-value is at most alpha is at most alpha

proofEntries.label: Remark 5.9
proofEntries.title: The plus-one correction is mandatory
proofEntries.statement: Zero observed exceedances do not justify p = 0; rejection at level alpha requires R + 1 >= 1/alpha, and the candidate count does not multiply this one-layer resolution requirement.
proofSteps: Read the minimum p-value directly from the corrected numerator and denominator.
proofEntries.conclusion: Randomization resolution is explicit and auditable.
proofEntries.boundary: Increasing the candidate family still affects the statistic's distribution even though it does not multiply the p-value grid requirement.

equations.alt: R plus one must be at least one over alpha

proofEntries.label: Proposition 5.10
proofEntries.title: Monte Carlo power transfer
proofEntries.statement: If the full-orbit p-value is at most gamma < alpha with probability at least 1 - beta, Monte Carlo power is at least one minus beta minus the explicit binomial tail for crossing alpha(R + 1).
assumptions: A full-orbit p-value margin gamma < alpha
proofSteps: Conditional on data, the exceedance count is Binomial(R,p(D)).
On p(D) <= gamma it is stochastically dominated by Binomial(R,gamma).
Union-bound failure of the full-orbit margin and the binomial resolution event.
proofEntries.conclusion: R can be selected from a target additional power loss, not by an informal 'large enough' rule.
proofEntries.boundary: The proposition transfers an established full-orbit margin; it does not create that margin.

equations.alt: Monte Carlo power is at least one minus beta minus an explicit binomial tail

proofEntries.label: Assumption 6.1
proofEntries.title: Balanced Gaussian two-sample model
proofEntries.statement: The two independent samples are centered Gaussian, both group proportions stay in a fixed interval away from zero, every baseline block covariance is positive definite, and each current-to-baseline relative covariance is uniformly bounded above and below.
proofSteps: This reference experiment fixes the balance and relative-conditioning constants used throughout the concentration and minimax arguments.
proofEntries.conclusion: All rate constants may depend on the fixed balance and relative-conditioning bounds, but not on n, p or the block family.
proofEntries.boundary: The condition does not require a well-conditioned raw baseline covariance; it constrains the relative change after whitening.

equations.alt: the relative current covariance lies between one over K and K times the identity

proofEntries.label: Assumption 6.2
proofEntries.title: Moderate-dimensional range
proofEntries.statement: For every candidate block and each tail parameter used by the proof, dimension plus weighted entropy plus tail size is no larger than a sufficiently small constant times the effective sample size.
proofSteps: This is the invertibility and perturbation regime for the sample pooled covariance.
proofEntries.conclusion: Second-order covariance concentration remains controlled uniformly over the candidate family.
proofEntries.boundary: The proportional b/n regime requires separate random-matrix asymptotics and is not covered.

equations.alt: block size plus entropy plus tail parameter is at most c zero times effective sample size

proofEntries.label: Lemma 6.3
proofEntries.title: Local concentration of the observed Gaussian contrast
proofEntries.statement: On a fixed block, the observed leading PWR root falls below the population root by more than a constant times r_ne(b,t+1) with probability at most 2e^{-t}.
proofSteps: Move to population pooled coordinates.
Concentrate both group covariance errors in operator norm.
Control inverse-square-root perturbation of the sample whitener.
Apply Weyl's inequality to the largest eigenvalue.
proofEntries.conclusion: The true block score has an explicit high-probability signal lower bound.
proofEntries.boundary: Constants rely on Gaussianity, group balance and bounded relative covariance.

equations.alt: the observed root is below the population root minus its concentration radius with probability at most two e to minus t

proofEntries.label: Lemma 6.4
proofEntries.title: Gaussian random-partition maximum scan
proofEntries.statement: For a uniform label reassignment independent of the data, the normalized maximum scan exceeds a constant multiple of its tail inflation factor with joint probability at most 2e^{-t}, even under the bounded Gaussian alternative.
assumptions: Uniform random assignment independent of data
proofSteps: Express the permuted covariance difference exactly as a centered finite-population matrix sum.
Control hypergeometric imbalance of original group membership.
Condition on the assignment and concentrate non-identically distributed Gaussian quadratic forms over a net.
Transfer population to sample pooled whitening and use the weighted union bound over overlapping blocks.
proofEntries.conclusion: Random partition erases the O(tau) signal up to hypergeometric leakage and matrix fluctuation on the same a_B scale.
proofEntries.boundary: The lemma is a joint data-permutation tail, not a pointwise deterministic bound for every conditional permutation quantile.

equations.alt: the joint probability that the randomized scan exceeds C two kappa t is at most two e to minus t

proofEntries.label: Remark 6.5
proofEntries.title: The new proof ingredient
proofEntries.statement: The nonstandard step is simultaneous control of hypergeometric signal leakage and matrix fluctuation after repartitioning two different Gaussian populations, uniformly over overlapping generalized-eigenvalue blocks.
proofSteps: Identify which ingredients are standard and isolate the random-partition maximum-scan bridge.
proofEntries.conclusion: Lemma 6.4 closes the gap between the actual permutation threshold and the analytic minimax scale.
proofEntries.boundary: Generic permutation-power results do not automatically imply this nonsmooth overlapping-block eigenvalue bound.

proofEntries.label: Theorem 6.6
proofEntries.title: Finite-sample permutation power lower bound
proofEntries.statement: If one true block's pooled population root exceeds the sum of its observed-contrast concentration radius and the normalized random-partition threshold, the full-orbit PWR test has power at least 1 - beta, subject to orbit resolution.
assumptions: Positive population effect on a candidate block
proofSteps: Lemma 6.3 puts the observed score above a fixed threshold with failure beta/2.
Use Lemma 6.4 and Fubini to bound the expected non-identity conditional orbit tail.
Markov's inequality converts the joint tail into a high-probability conditional tail.
Combine the identity mass and residual orbit budget to obtain p <= alpha.
proofEntries.conclusion: The actual full-permutation test, not a surrogate analytic scan, receives a finite-sample power guarantee.
proofEntries.boundary: The constants are non-sharp and the theorem remains inside the balanced Gaussian moderate-dimensional regime.

equations.alt: a separated population root implies power at least one minus beta

proofEntries.label: Remark 6.7
proofEntries.title: Orbit resolution
proofEntries.statement: The full-permutation p-value cannot be smaller than one over the orbit size, so |G|^{-1} <= alpha is necessary for rejection; in a balanced two-sample orbit this condition becomes automatic quickly as N grows.
proofSteps: Read the minimum p-value from the identity assignment's unavoidable exceedance.
proofEntries.conclusion: The theorem reserves the usable alpha budget after accounting for the identity mass.
proofEntries.boundary: A tiny orbit can make a formally valid test unable to reject.

proofEntries.label: Remark 6.8
proofEntries.title: Why the Markov step matters
proofEntries.statement: Power depends on a data-conditional permutation tail, whereas Lemma 6.4 is joint in data and permutation; Markov's inequality is the explicit bridge from the joint expectation to the high-probability conditional bound.
proofSteps: Apply Fubini to identify the expected conditional tail, then Markov to control its realized value.
proofEntries.conclusion: An analogy between analytic and permutation thresholds cannot replace this conditioning step.
proofEntries.boundary: The conversion is conservative and does not yield a sharp conditional quantile approximation.

proofEntries.label: Corollary 6.9
proofEntries.title: Moderate-regime detection condition
proofEntries.statement: For fixed alpha, beta, balance and relative-conditioning constants, uniform moderate dimension and sufficient orbit resolution reduce Theorem 6.6 to the square-root direction plus square-root search rate.
proofSteps: Tail parameters are fixed constants.
The kappa inflation is bounded.
Absorb the second-order term into the two square-root terms.
proofEntries.conclusion: A sufficiently large constant times sqrt(b/n_e) + sqrt(ell/n_e) yields power at least 1 - beta.
proofEntries.boundary: This is a rate statement; it does not supply a sharp finite-sample constant.

equations.alt: the signal is at least a constant times the square root dimension rate plus square root entropy rate

proofEntries.label: Corollary 6.10
proofEntries.title: Finite Monte Carlo power
proofEntries.statement: Replacing alpha by a strict margin gamma in Theorem 6.6 and applying Proposition 5.10 yields full finite-sample Monte Carlo power minus an explicit binomial tail.
assumptions: Theorem 6.6 separation at the gamma margin
proofSteps: Establish a full-orbit p-value margin at gamma.
Transfer it through the conditional binomial exceedance count.
proofEntries.conclusion: The permutation budget R can be tied to a stated power-loss tolerance.
proofEntries.boundary: The locked V2 campaign needed to estimate operational constants remains pending.

proofEntries.label: Theorem 6.11
proofEntries.title: Minimax lower bound for unknown direction and location
proofEntries.statement: Even when the baseline covariance is known and only the current Gaussian sample must be tested, total risk stays bounded away from zero when theta is below a constant times max{sqrt(b/n_1), sqrt(log M/n_1)} over M disjoint candidate blocks.
assumptions: M pairwise-disjoint blocks of width b
Rank-one positive spike in the small-signal range theta < 1
proofSteps: Unknown direction: mix the spike direction uniformly on the b-sphere and bound chi-square divergence when n theta^2/b is small.
Unknown location: mix fixed orthogonal directions over M disjoint blocks and bound divergence when n theta^2 <= c log M.
Use Le Cam's inequality in each subexperiment and take the harder of the two costs.
proofEntries.conclusion: No test uniformly beats both the direction and location square-root costs.
proofEntries.boundary: The theorem is a rate lower bound with universal constants, not a sharp power envelope.

equations.alt: below the maximum of direction and location rates, minimax total risk stays at least c zero

proofEntries.label: Theorem 6.12
proofEntries.title: Balanced Gaussian minimax rate
proofEntries.statement: With comparable group sizes, M equal-width candidates weighted 1/M, moderate dimension and a disjoint packing, the actual full-permutation PWR-Scan attains the minimax rank-one separation rate sqrt(b/n) + sqrt(log M/n), up to constant factors.
assumptions: Candidate family contains the lower-bound packing
proofSteps: Balance makes n_e, n and n_1 equivalent up to constants.
The monotone pooled effect is equivalent to the bounded baseline spike.
Corollary 6.9 supplies the upper rate; Theorem 6.11 supplies max of the same two terms.
Use max{x,y} <= x+y <= 2 max{x,y}.
proofEntries.conclusion: The same permutation-calibrated statistic that is exact under the null is rate-optimal in the Gaussian reference experiment.
proofEntries.boundary: No uniformly most-powerful, sharp-constant, proportional-dimensional or non-Gaussian optimality claim is made.

equations.alt: the minimax separation rate is square root b over n plus square root log M over n

proofEntries.label: Remark 6.13
proofEntries.title: What rate optimality does not say
proofEntries.statement: Theorem 6.12 establishes order and fixed-factor equivalence only; it does not imply uniform most-powerfulness, a sharp asymptotic constant, a power envelope, or optimality beyond independent balanced Gaussian moderate dimension.
proofSteps: Separate rate equivalence from stronger optimality notions.
proofEntries.conclusion: The public claim is deliberately narrower than 'optimal in all settings'.
proofEntries.boundary: Real-audio performance and external validity require empirical evidence, not extrapolation from this theorem.

proofEntries.label: Assumption 6.14
proofEntries.title: Approximate block spike
proofEntries.statement: On some candidate block, the population pooled contrast equals tau u u^T plus a symmetric remainder R whose operator norm is at most eta.
proofSteps: This assumption packages weak extra components, Taylor error, leakage and finite-taper error into one auditable norm bound.
proofEntries.conclusion: Model mismatch enters the power theorem through a single conservative signal erosion eta.
proofEntries.boundary: Eta must be bounded externally; describing leakage as merely 'small' is not sufficient.

equations.alt: the population contrast equals a rank-one signal plus an operator norm bounded remainder

proofEntries.label: Theorem 6.15
proofEntries.title: Mismatch-robust permutation power
proofEntries.statement: Under the Gaussian and moderate-dimensional assumptions plus an approximate spike, Theorem 6.6 remains valid after replacing the nominal signal by (tau - eta)+.
proofSteps: Weyl's inequality lower-bounds the population leading eigenvalue by tau - eta.
All subsequent concentration and random-partition arguments use only that population lower bound.
proofEntries.conclusion: The finite-sample power guarantee degrades explicitly with operator-norm mismatch.
proofEntries.boundary: When eta >= tau the theorem guarantees no positive signal and no favorable power claim is justified.

equations.alt: effective signal is the positive part of tau minus eta and yields power at least one minus beta under the separation condition

proofEntries.label: Theorem 7.1
proofEntries.title: Deterministic interval covering
proofEntries.statement: Every admissible contiguous interval is contained in a member of the shifted geometric candidate family whose length is less than 2(1 + epsilon) times the true interval length.
assumptions: Grid spacing at most epsilon times the scale width
proofSteps: Choose the smallest geometric scale at least as wide as the target interval, making it less than twice the target width.
Choose the last shifted grid start not exceeding the target start.
The start mismatch is below one grid step, so the enlarged candidate covers the target while its length obeys the stated factor.
proofEntries.conclusion: An O(p)-scale deterministic family covers every interval without data-dependent screening.
proofEntries.boundary: A single aligned dyadic tree does not provide this uniform constant-factor covering for intervals crossing a tree boundary.

equations.alt: I is contained in B of I and the covering block is less than two times one plus epsilon times the interval size

proofEntries.label: Lemma 7.2
proofEntries.title: PSD signal monotonicity under supersets
proofEntries.statement: If a positive-semidefinite covariance increase is supported inside I x I and I is contained in B, the leading pooled-whitened population root on B is at least its value on I.
assumptions: Support contained in the true interval
proofSteps: Write the leading root as a generalized Rayleigh maximum on B.
Restrict candidate vectors to zero outside I.
On this subset, numerator and denominator equal the I-block Rayleigh quotient.
proofEntries.conclusion: Covering enlarges noise dimension but does not attenuate a strict PSD block signal.
proofEntries.boundary: An indefinite remainder must be handled separately through the eta mismatch bound.

equations.alt: the pooled leading root on the covering block is at least the leading root on the true interval

proofEntries.label: Theorem 7.3
proofEntries.title: Adaptive power of multiscale PWR-Scan
proofEntries.statement: Uniformly over admissible widths, a PSD interval signal is detected with power at least 1 - beta when its population PWR effect exceeds the direction, location, scale-adaptation and second-order concentration terms induced by the shifted geometric family.
proofSteps: Select the constant-factor covering block from Theorem 7.1.
Use Lemma 7.2 to preserve the population effect.
Bound covering-block dimension and its weighted entropy by b and Lambda_b.
Insert those bounds into Theorem 6.6 and absorb constants.
proofEntries.conclusion: One permutation-calibrated multiscale maximum adapts over unknown interval width.
proofEntries.boundary: The theorem is an adaptive upper bound and does not prove that its log-log scale cost is information-theoretically necessary.

equations.alt: adaptive radius equals direction, adaptive entropy, and second-order terms; signal above a constant times this radius is detected

proofEntries.label: Corollary 7.4
proofEntries.title: Near-minimax width adaptation
proofEntries.statement: For fixed design constants and moderate dimension, multiscale PWR-Scan detects at the fixed-width direction-plus-location rate with an additional log-log term for unknown scale.
proofSteps: Bound the selected geometric scale by 1 + log2(b/b_min).
Substitute into Lambda_b and drop the lower-order second-order concentration term.
Compare with the fixed-width packing lower bound.
proofEntries.conclusion: Width adaptation costs at most a logarithm of the number of scales inside the square-root entropy term.
proofEntries.boundary: Removal or necessity of the adaptation term is an unresolved sharp-adaptation question.

equations.alt: the adaptive rate is square root b over n plus the square root of location entropy and twice log scale count over n

proofEntries.label: Lemma B.1
proofEntries.title: Gaussian covariance concentration on one block
proofEntries.statement: For m independent standard b-variate Gaussian vectors, the sample covariance differs from identity in operator norm by at most 2r + r^2 with probability at least 1 - 2e^{-t^2/2}, where r = sqrt(b/m) + t/sqrt(m).
proofSteps: Represent the covariance as m^{-1}G^T G.
Apply the extreme singular-value inequality to G.
Square the normalized singular-value interval and take its largest deviation from one.
proofEntries.conclusion: A nonasymptotic operator-norm radius is available block by block.
proofEntries.boundary: The standard statement assumes Gaussian observations and no data-dependent dimension choice.

equations.label: (B.4)
equations.alt: sample covariance error is at most two r plus r squared

proofEntries.label: Lemma B.2
proofEntries.title: Average of non-identical Gaussian covariances
proofEntries.statement: Independent centered Gaussian vectors with uniformly bounded covariance eigenvalues obey the same sqrt((b+x)/m) + (b+x)/m relative operator-norm concentration around their average covariance.
assumptions: Uniform upper and lower covariance bounds
proofSteps: For each fixed direction, centered Gaussian squares are uniformly sub-exponential.
Apply scalar Bernstein on a one-quarter net.
Lift the net maximum to operator norm.
proofEntries.conclusion: Permutation groups containing observations from both original populations remain concentrable after conditioning on membership.
proofEntries.boundary: Constants depend on the covariance condition ratio.

proofEntries.label: Lemma B.3
proofEntries.title: Weighted union bound
proofEntries.statement: If block event failures are bounded by c e^{-x}, evaluating block B at x + log(1/w_B) and summing weights no larger than one yields simultaneous success with probability at least 1 - c e^{-x}.
assumptions: Positive pre-fixed weights summing to at most one
proofSteps: Substitute the block-specific tail allocation.
Sum c e^{-x} w_B over blocks.
proofEntries.conclusion: Weighted entropy log(1/w_B) replaces a crude uniform log M cost.
proofEntries.boundary: Weights selected after seeing the tested data invalidate the registered event allocation.

equations.label: B.3 bound
equations.alt: all weighted block events hold with probability at least one minus c e to minus x

proofEntries.label: Lemma B.4
proofEntries.title: Pooled population gap for a Roy spike
proofEntries.statement: For a baseline-relative rank-one covariance spike of size theta, the pooled-whitened population contrast has one nonzero eigenvalue delta(theta) = theta/(1 + pi_1 theta).
proofSteps: Use congruence invariance to set the baseline covariance to identity.
Diagonalize along u and its orthogonal complement.
Read the unique whitened eigenvalue in the u direction.
proofEntries.conclusion: For bounded spikes, pooled and baseline-relative effect sizes are equivalent up to constants.
proofEntries.boundary: The mapping saturates under large spikes because the pooled denominator also grows.

equations.label: (B.5)
equations.alt: delta theta equals theta divided by one plus pi one theta

proofEntries.label: Lemma B.5
proofEntries.title: Signal-noise decomposition of the observed statistic
proofEntries.statement: On the true block, the observed largest PWR root exceeds the pooled population gap minus a constant times the Gaussian direction and second-order covariance-estimation errors with high probability.
proofSteps: Control the pooled covariance and group-difference errors.
Perturb the inverse square root under an operator-norm half-radius event.
Apply Weyl's inequality and insert Lemma B.4.
proofEntries.conclusion: The observed true-block root retains the population gap up to the stated nonasymptotic radius.
proofEntries.boundary: This appendix form targets constant-factor rates, not optimized constants.

equations.label: (B.6)
equations.alt: the observed true block statistic exceeds the population gap minus its covariance concentration error

proofEntries.label: Lemma B.6
proofEntries.title: Joint tail of the permuted PWR-Scan
proofEntries.statement: Under the Gaussian null or bounded-spike alternative and the appendix common conditions, the data-and-reassignment joint upper tail of the normalized scan is bounded by a sub-Gaussian term plus an exponentially small effective-sample term.
assumptions: Gaussian null or bounded spike alternative
proofSteps: Condition on the hypergeometric mixture count.
Apply non-identical Gaussian covariance concentration to each permuted group.
Allocate tails over candidates with Lemma B.3.
Absorb population mixture imbalance and whitener perturbation into the same scale.
proofEntries.conclusion: A joint tail strong enough for the full-orbit power proof holds without approximating the entire conditional permutation CDF.
proofEntries.boundary: It is not a deterministic upper bound on every data-conditional permutation quantile.

equations.label: (B.9)
equations.alt: the joint permuted scan tail is bounded by two exponential terms

proofEntries.label: Remark B.7
proofEntries.title: A joint tail is sufficient
proofEntries.statement: The proof deliberately avoids claiming a deterministic conditional permutation threshold; Fubini converts the full-orbit p-value expectation into the joint tail needed for minimax power.
proofSteps: Restrict the proof target to the rejection probability actually required.
proofEntries.conclusion: The weaker joint statement closes the power chain without an unnecessary conditional-CDF theorem.
proofEntries.boundary: It should not be advertised as uniform conditional quantile control.

proofEntries.label: Theorem B.8
proofEntries.title: Joint-tail proof of full-orbit power
proofEntries.statement: Under the appendix common conditions and adequate orbit resolution, a true-block pooled gap above a constant times sqrt(b/n_eff) + sqrt(log(1/w_B)/n_eff) gives full-orbit power at least 1 - beta for sufficiently large n_eff.
proofSteps: Put the observed statistic above a fixed threshold using Lemma B.5.
Bound the non-identity joint orbit tail using Lemma B.6.
Apply Markov to the conditional non-identity tail.
Add identity mass and the residual orbit budget to obtain p_G <= alpha.
proofEntries.conclusion: The actual full-orbit PWR-Scan obtains the fixed-scale power upper bound.
proofEntries.boundary: The theorem states a constant-factor moderate-dimensional rate, not a sharp constant.

equations.label: (B.11)
equations.alt: the pooled gap is above the direction and weighted search rates

proofEntries.label: Proposition B.9
proofEntries.title: Operator-norm mismatch
proofEntries.statement: If the true pooled contrast is delta u u^T + E with ||E||op <= eta, its leading eigenvalue is at least delta - eta, so Theorem B.8 applies with (delta - eta)+.
proofSteps: Evaluate the Rayleigh quotient at u.
Lower-bound u^T E u by -||E||op.
Substitute the resulting population gap into the observed lower-bound proof.
proofEntries.conclusion: Mismatch subtracts at most its operator norm from the usable signal.
proofEntries.boundary: No positive gap remains guaranteed when eta is at least delta.

equations.label: B.9 bound
equations.alt: the maximum eigenvalue is at least delta minus eta

appendixSections.label: B.1
appendixSections.title: Common conditions
coreSteps: Fix balanced group proportions, bounded pooled eigenvalues and a bounded spike range.
Require pre-fixed weights summing to at most one and uniform moderate dimension.

appendixSections.label: B.2
appendixSections.title: Gaussian sample covariance concentration
coreSteps: Establish standard and non-identical Gaussian operator-norm concentration.

appendixSections.label: B.3
appendixSections.title: Uniform concentration over candidates
coreSteps: Allocate tail probability by pre-fixed candidate weights.

appendixSections.label: B.4
appendixSections.title: Pooled population gap of a rank-one spike
coreSteps: Diagonalize along the spike direction after baseline whitening.

appendixSections.label: B.5
appendixSections.title: Observed true-block lower bound
coreSteps: Combine covariance concentration, whitener perturbation and Weyl's inequality.

appendixSections.label: B.6
appendixSections.title: Why random reassignment erases the signal
coreSteps: The number of original current observations in the permuted current group is hypergeometric.
Its centered composition coefficient is O_P(n_eff^{-1/2}), reducing an O(theta) signal to O_P(theta/sqrt(n_eff)).

appendixSections.label: B.7
appendixSections.title: Joint randomization tail
coreSteps: Control the data-and-randomization joint tail rather than the full conditional CDF.

appendixSections.label: B.8
appendixSections.title: Power of the full-orbit p-value
coreSteps: Use Fubini, a threshold event and Markov's inequality to control the actual orbit rank.

appendixSections.label: B.9
appendixSections.title: Monte Carlo randomization power loss
coreSteps: Conditional exceedances are binomial.
A Chernoff bound gives R of order alpha^{-1} log(2/beta), not M/alpha.

appendixSections.label: B.10
appendixSections.title: Power under an approximate spike
coreSteps: Replace the nominal pooled gap by its positive part after subtracting operator-norm mismatch.

appendixSections.label: B.11
appendixSections.title: Two parts of the minimax lower bound
coreSteps: Prove impossibility in an easier known-baseline oracle experiment and combine direction and location mixtures.

appendixSections.label: B.11.1
appendixSections.title: Unknown direction
coreSteps: Mix directions uniformly on the sphere.
Bound chi-square divergence when n theta^2/b is small and invoke Le Cam.

appendixSections.label: B.11.2
appendixSections.title: Unknown location
coreSteps: Mix one fixed direction over disjoint blocks.
Bound chi-square divergence when n theta^2 <= c log K and invoke Le Cam.

appendixSections.label: B.12
appendixSections.title: Scope of the proof
coreSteps: The proof closes for fixed or label-independent centering, balanced Gaussian features, moderate dimension, positive covariance increase, pre-fixed candidates and full-orbit or sufficiently accurate Monte Carlo calibration.
Group-specific centering, selected ridge, heavy tails, proportional dimension and a single dependent time series require new theory.

claimsBoundary: The manuscript establishes mathematical implications only under their displayed assumptions.
The 56 engineering runs and 246 computational tests verify calculation paths; they are not a statistical power sample size.
External validity is not established, and the negative DCASE result is retained without reinterpretation.
The source PDF is intentionally not included in the production artifact.
